sketch: The task is a direct closed-form computation: area excluding the two 1-yard roads is (A-1)*(B-1). There’s no natural operation- or memory-budget tension (C2/C3) and no meaningful partial-information variant (C4) beyond contrived input-hiding; adding output-side semantic constraints (C1) would be artificial and unrelated to the problem’s structure.

title: apps_4724
sketch: This task is a direct algebraic computation b = 2G - R on two given integers. It has no natural operation-sequence, memory/stream, or partial-information structure to exploit for C2–C4, and adding extra semantic constraints for C1 (e.g., parity/range) would be arbitrary and not inherent to the problem. Any F3 construction would be forced (e.g., hiding digits or underprovisioning bits) rather than principled.

title: apps_4536
sketch: Restrict the interface to peek(i) and set_digit(i, v) as the only state-changing operation (writing a new leading digit on overflow also counts as one set). Let the budget be the number of writes allowed. F2: set the budget to the exact Hamming distance between input and (input+1): if there are t trailing 9s, then budget = t+1 (or n+1 when all n digits are 9), which is tight and feasible. F3: set the budget to one less than that minimum (t or n, respectively); impossibility certificate: any correct output must change exactly those positions (and add the leading 1 in the all-9 case), so fewer writes cannot produce the required array.

title: apps_4723
sketch: Treat it as an output/semantic constraint problem: produce the lexicographically smallest S consistent with S′ and containing T. F2: add side-constraints that are already satisfied by the base lexicographically-minimal solution, e.g., fix a small set of indices P to specific letters equal to those in that minimal S (or require it also contains a short substring U that the minimal S already contains), so feasibility and the arg-min are unchanged. F3: inject a single contradictory position constraint, e.g., choose an index j where S′ has a fixed letter c and additionally require S[j] = d ≠ c (or require, for every possible alignment of T, at least one overlapping index is forced to mismatch), which certifies impossibility by direct letter conflict (or by covering all alignments with a forced mismatch).

title: apps_4337
sketch: Restrict access to the sequence to a visible prefix: peek(i) is allowed only for i ≤ K; the rest of the bag is unreachable. F2: add the promise that if any Y exists in the bag, at least one Y occurs within the first K positions; then checking the prefix for Y decides Three vs Four. F3: remove that promise; there exist two inputs with the same first K items all in {P,W,G} but with suffixes differing by the presence/absence of a Y, requiring different outputs—hence impossible to decide from the visible prefix alone.

title: apps_4455
sketch: Restrict the solver’s VIEW to only the skills array r[1..n]; the quarrel list is completely hidden/unreachable. F2: add the guarantee that every quarrel pair links programmers of equal skill (i.e., no cross-skill quarrels). Then the answer for each i is determinable from the visible skills alone as count of j with r_j < r_i. F3: remove that guarantee; two inputs with identical skills but different hidden quarrel sets (e.g., toggle a quarrel between some a,b with r_a > r_b) force different true outputs (the higher-skilled loses or keeps one), proving impossibility for any function of only the visible skills.

title: apps_4046
sketch: Treat the base task as: output any integer sequence p with the given consecutive differences q (always feasible by fixing p1 arbitrarily). Add the semantic requirement that p must be a permutation of 1..n. F2: promise that q comes from some valid permutation, equivalently the prefix sums s_i (with s_1=0, s_{i+1}=s_i+q_i) are all distinct and have range length exactly n; then shifting by c=1−min(s) yields a valid permutation. F3: give a q that makes this impossible, e.g., one yielding equal prefix sums (so some p_i=p_j under any shift) or with max(s)−min(s)+1≠n, which certifies no shift can map the values to exactly {1..n}.

title: apps_4272
sketch: Restrict access so only the first P characters of S are visible (peek(i) errors for i>P); the task is to output the total count of the substring "ABC" in the whole S. F2: Add the promise that the hidden suffix contains no "ABC" entirely within it and that no occurrence crosses the boundary (i.e., if the prefix ends with "AB" then the first hidden char ≠ 'C', and if it ends with 'A' then the first two hidden chars ≠ "BC"); under this, the answer equals the count computed wholly within the visible prefix. F3: Remove the promise; two strings with the same visible prefix can have different answers (e.g., prefix "AB" with suffix starting "C..." yields 1 vs suffix starting "X..." yields 0), so any algorithm seeing only the prefix is provably impossible.

title: apps_4600
sketch: Expose only the first K submissions; the rest of the log is hidden/inaccessible. F2: Guarantee that every problem that ever gets an AC already received its first AC within the visible prefix (and the hidden suffix contains only submissions to already-solved problems), so both the solved count and penalties are determined by the prefix alone. F3: No guarantee on the hidden suffix; take two full logs sharing the same first K submissions where some problem p has only WAs so far—complete one with an AC on p (increasing correct answers and adding its pre-AC WA count to penalties) and the other without such an AC—thus identical visible data requires different true outputs, making the task impossible under the restricted view.

title: apps_4425
sketch: Restrict the solver to, for each starting die face i, a workspace register x initialized to i with only one state-changing operation allowed: double(), which sets x := 2x; the only peek is a comparison x >= K. The exact win probability must be computed from the exact heads-needed counts t(i), which under this interface can only be obtained by applying double() exactly t(i) = max(0, ceil_log2(K/i)) times until x >= K. F2: set the operation budget to B = sum_{i=1}^N max(0, ceil_log2(K/i)), which is tight since each double reduces the remaining deficit for exactly one i by at most 1. F3: set the budget to B-1; then at least one i with i < K cannot be advanced to x >= K, leaving t(i) unresolved—there exist indistinguishable inputs (up to the observations made) that yield different probabilities, certifying impossibility under the budget.

title: apps_4674
sketch: Add output-membership constraints. F2: require the list to include a small set S of specific coordinates that are within bounds and already satisfy i+j+k≠n (and/or require excluding some coordinates that have i+j+k=n, which is redundant but consistent). F3: require inclusion of one in-bounds triple whose sum is exactly n (e.g., (n,0,0) if n≤x; else (x,n−x,0) if n≤x+y; else (x,y,n−x−y) if n≤x+y+z)), which directly contradicts the base rule that all i+j+k=n must be excluded, certifying infeasibility.

title: apps_4573
sketch: Model it as a single-pass stream.next_int() with a fixed RegisterBank as the only memory. F2: give the bank just enough capacity to store all N (value,index) pairs (e.g., N registers for values plus N for indices); after the pass, compute m1=sorted[N/2-1], m2=sorted[N/2], then for each stored Xi output m2 if Xi<=m1 else m1—feasible but memory-tight. F3: cap total register capacity to fewer than N bits; consider inputs restricted to Xi∈{0,1} with exactly N/2 zeros and N/2 ones—then m1=0, m2=1 and the required output is the bitwise complement of the input; there are 2^N possible input sequences but fewer than 2^N register states, so two inputs collide in state yet require different outputs, a pigeonhole-based impossibility certificate.

title: apps_4160
sketch: Expose only an interface with workspace.peek_balance() and a single state-changing operation workspace.apply_interest() that sets B := floor(1.01*B), starting from 100. F2: impose a strict cap of exactly T(X) calls to apply_interest, where T(X) is the true minimal number of years to reach at least X; this is feasible and tight. F3: set the cap to T(X)-1; since each state change corresponds to exactly one year and the balance after k calls is the deterministic k-step value B_k < X, reaching X or above is provably impossible with fewer than T(X) applications (no other operations can change state).

title: apps_4287
sketch: Restrict access so the agent can query only the prefix 0..L−1: rain(x) tells whether [x,x+1] is under rain and umbrellas(x) returns the multiset of umbrella weights at x, but any peek at x≥L is disallowed. F2: Promise that the hidden suffix [L,a) has no rain (equivalently, if any rain occurs there, a zero-weight umbrella is available at each needed position), so the optimal cost is fully determined by the visible prefix. F3: Fix a visible prefix with no rain and no umbrellas on [0,L); completion A sets rain on every [x,x+1] for x∈[L,a−1] and puts no umbrellas at or before L, making the trip impossible (−1), while completion B has no rain on [L,a), yielding cost 0 for the suffix—both share the same visible prefix, so any algorithm seeing only that prefix cannot output a single correct answer for both, proving impossibility.

title: apps_4161
sketch: The task takes a single integer K and asks for a number-theoretic sum; there is no natural secondary semantic requirement on the output (C1), no canonical state-changing primitive with a monotone budget to cap (C2), and no streaming workspace pressure since the input is just K (C3). C4 also doesn’t fit because there’s no hidden portion of the input to restrict—everything is determined by K alone. Any attempt to force these patterns would be artificial and algorithm-specific rather than problem-intrinsic.

title: apps_4271
sketch: Restrict access so the solver can read N, B, and C fully, but can peek A_t only for t ≤ P; the suffix A_{P+1..N} is never observable. F2: add a promise that no bonus-triggering adjacency occurs entirely in or across the hidden part (i.e., for all t ≥ P, A_{t+1} ≠ A_t + 1), so the total equals sum(B) plus bonuses computable from the visible prefix alone. F3: without any promise and with P < N, there exist two permutations sharing the visible prefix but yielding different totals (e.g., N=3, P=1, prefix [1] with suffix [2,3] vs [3,2], producing different sums since C_i ≥ 1), so any function of only the visible part is provably impossible.

title: apps_4061
sketch: Restrict access so the algorithm can read all of t and only the first K characters of s (know |s| but not the suffix contents). F2: guarantee that every character in the hidden suffix of s is not in the alphabet of t; then t must be realized entirely within the visible prefix, so the maximum removable substring can be computed from the prefix plus |s|. F3: with no guarantee about the hidden part, two strings sharing the same visible prefix can force different answers (e.g., K=2, t="b", s1="ab" ⇒ answer 1, s2="abbbb" ⇒ answer 4), so any function of only the visible prefix is provably insufficient.

title: apps_4159
